items.prose: Blending two parts reactive volcanic pumice ash with one part aged slaked lime created a self-healing hydraulic mortar. The mixture hardened underwater inside the flooded aquifer intake tunnel, reaching eighteen megapascals strength in ninety days.

Milling scavenged clay roofing tiles into 2mm ceramic grog and blending with hydraulic lime produced a pink, watertight *opus signinum* plaster. The lining sealed the primary 50,000-gallon drinking water reservoir without shrinking or cracking.

Spherical glassy fly ash particles raked from boiler precipitator hoppers replaced 30% of Portland cement in the turbine pedestal mass pour. The pozzolanic reaction consumed calcium hydroxide, preventing alkali-silica reaction and lowering curing heat.

High-alumina mortar applied to repair a geothermal sump wall was attacked by dissolved sulfate ions. Formation of needle-like ettringite crystals exerted massive internal crystallization pressure, heaving mortar joints 20mm and spalling brick faces.

Whipping dehydrated egg albumen and rendered beef blood into slaked lime mortar generated micro-air bubbles and hydrophobic protein cross-links. Applied across vault roof masonry, it completely repelled acidic seepage water.

Using crushed cellular volcanic tufa in place of dense granite gravel reduced concrete density from 2,400 kg/m³ to 1,350 kg/m³. The lightweight concrete allowed overhead sentry walkways to span twenty meters without intermediate structural steel pillars.

Mortar joints in the surface lookout turret lacked air-entraining soap agents. Trapped pore water froze during a -30°C winter cold snap; water expansion peeled the outer 15mm of mortar off like pie crust, loosening parapet stone blocks.

Heavy three-inch steel hinge pins for the outer blast door were anchored into solid basalt bedrock using molten brimstone sulfur mixed with lead grit. The sulfur solidified into rock-hard matrix in ninety seconds, withstanding 50-ton hinge shear loads.
